Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

the next visit to wren hall is for the scheduled room inspection on the twenty first not for another scan session dev will take the humidity reading, check the cabinet card, and report whether the basement room is below the stated limit if it is above sixty percent the blue case stays closed and he contacts me before handling any cassette the rehearsal groups have not asked for copies at this stage and there is no new booking request in the hall diary the binder remains on the archive shelf beside the recorder cabinet and the key register stays in the locked drawer until the room inspection", "output": "This is Mara Ellis, recording the handoff notes for the North Room rehearsal archive on Monday the twelfth of May. The main thing I am doing today is forwarding the reference files and the paper log scans to the Harbor Sound Library. The rehearsal archive has been kept in the basement room at Wren Hall since the building renovation in twenty twenty-one, and the collection covers the brass ensemble and the youth theatre company from twenty sixteen through last winter. We have forty-two labeled audio files and eleven folders of related documents. The oldest audio file is on a compact disc, and the newest one is a WAV file from February this year. The two groups used the same room, but they had separate booking sheets, so the names and dates need to stay attached to the right folder.

On Friday I checked the box against the shelf list with Dev Patel, who looks after the room keys and the small recorder cabinet. We found thirty-eight cassettes, two mini discs, and four memory cards in the blue case. The cassette labels use pencil, and some are difficult to read, but every label is legible in the close photographs. The shelf list also records three rehearsal dates that were changed by the hall manager, so those dates are not evidence that a session took place. The paper log has a note from Jo Wren saying the youth theatre left the room at six on the seventeenth and the brass group came in after seven. Jo wrote that the door was still unlocked when she returned for her scarf, and that detail is why the key register is included with the other scans.

Numbered notes for the transfer. Item one: the folder called North Room Brass includes rehearsal plans for the winter concert. Item two: the folder called Youth Theatre includes a running order and a cast list with phone numbers covered before the copy was made. Item three: the small envelope marked Room Tone has two audio files and a handwritten note that says, “Do not reduce the low hum because it is part of the room recording.” The note is signed by Lena Cho, who recorded the files. Item four: the blue case inventory has one blank line where the last memory card should have a description. The card itself is marked “April lobby,” and I have kept that wording rather than guessing what lobby means. The archive reference for this transfer is HS North 24 051, and the scan folder uses the same reference.

Ravi at the Harbor Sound Library asked for the files in their original folder order and for the log pages to remain separate from the rehearsal plans. I am forwarding a copy of the shelf list as well as the scans because the list gives the date and location for each item. The first page of the log is folded across the lower right corner, but the words are visible, and I have not flattened it on the scanner. The scanner glass picked up a faint line on the next page, and the line appears in the image too. The paper is cream rather than white, so the background looks darker than the pages in the newer folder. Nothing has been removed from the scan set, and the two pages with personal phone numbers are the versions with those numbers covered.

When Dev and I packed the drives on Monday morning, we made one transfer folder for the audio and one for the documents. The audio folder contains WAV copies and a checksum sheet. The checksum sheet lists the source filename, the copy filename, the file size, and the date of the copy. The original names are retained in a column because two files have the same rehearsal date but different start times. The document folder contains the photographed cassette labels, the booking sheets, the key register, the shelf list, and the log pages. The rehearsal plans are filed after the related booking sheet rather than by the date they were scanned. That arrangement follows the order on the shelf list and should make it possible to compare the paper records with the audio filenames.

There is a condition that matters before anyone opens the blue case again. If the basement room has a humidity reading above sixty percent, leave the case closed and contact Dev before taking out a cassette. The monitor showed fifty-four percent when we checked on Friday, but Dev said the basement reading can rise after heavy rain. The next room inspection is scheduled for the twenty-first of May, and the reading should be written on the cabinet card even if the room looks dry. This instruction applies to the cassettes and mini discs in the blue case. It does not apply to the two drives that are already in the locked drawer. Dev has the drawer key, and the key register records when that key is signed out.

Ravi said, “We can match the scans to the shelf list before we add the collection to the catalogue, and the original folder order will help us explain the rehearsal dates.” He also asked that we include a note about the covered numbers so staff do not mistake those copies for missing pages. I have put that note beside the scan manifest rather than on the log itself. The manifest identifies the source folder, the scan date, and the number of pages in each file. It does not describe the content of every page because some pages have no heading and the handwriting is too faint to read from a thumbnail. The full-size images are in the document folder, and the audio filenames are in the checksum sheet.

This afternoon I am forwarding the two folders and the reference sheet through the library's transfer link. The link address came from Ravi's message dated the ninth of May, and Dev checked that the address matches the one in the handoff email. The package is not being sent to the public catalogue inbox. The note to the receiving staff asks them to confirm that both folders arrived and to tell us if a filename does not match the checksum sheet. It does not ask them to rename files or to combine the folders. I have saved a copy of the handoff email with the archive paperwork and written the transfer date on the inside of the North Room binder.

The next visit to Wren Hall is for the scheduled room inspection on the twenty-first, not for another scan session. Dev will take the humidity reading, check the cabinet card, and report whether the basement room is below the stated limit. If it is above sixty percent, the blue case stays closed and he contacts me before handling any cassette. The rehearsal groups have not asked for copies at this stage, and there is no new booking request in the hall diary. The binder remains on the archive shelf beside the recorder cabinet, and the key register stays in the locked drawer until the room inspection."}]
